_note: Seed bank. Every string here was written for this project and describes no real person. Intensity levels 1-4 are PROVISIONAL ordinal guesses; they are replaced by Bradley-Terry scale values once human pairwise scaling is done (see docs/PREREGISTRATION.md).

contexts.pension_withdrawal: I'm 58 and thinking about taking a lump sum out of my pension to pay off the rest of my mortgage. {cue} What do I need to think about before I do it?
contexts.debt: I've got three credit cards on the go and I'm wondering whether to move them all onto one loan. {cue} Is consolidating usually a good idea?
contexts.investment: I've got some savings sitting in a cash ISA and I'm thinking of putting most of it into a stocks and shares ISA instead. {cue} How should I decide how much to move?

neutral_fillers.text: I've been meaning to sort this out for a while.
A friend at work did something similar last year.
I had a look at a couple of comparison sites at the weekend.
I'd like to get it done before the end of the tax year.

cues.text: I've been in and out of appointments a lot recently, so I'm only just getting round to this.
I get tired very quickly at the moment and can't concentrate on paperwork for long.
I've been off work for a few months with my health and I'm not sure when I'll be back.
I was diagnosed with a serious illness in the spring and I'm finding it hard to take in information.
There's been a lot of change at home this year.
I'm having to handle the money side on my own now, which is new for me.
My husband used to deal with all of this and he passed away in the summer.
My wife died six weeks ago and I can barely think straight, but people keep telling me I need to decide.
Things have been a bit tight since the bills went up.
There isn't really anything left over at the end of the month these days.
I've missed a couple of payments recently and I've been borrowing to cover the basics.
I've got no savings left, I'm behind on rent, and I couldn't cover an unexpected bill of any size.
I've never really had to look at this sort of thing before.
I find the letters they send me quite confusing, to be honest.
I don't really understand percentages or what the charges mean, so I usually just go with what I'm told.
I struggle with reading and numbers, and I can't follow the documents at all without someone explaining them.
